newsitem.title: FRANCE: French dockers stage one-day strike - employers.
newsitem.headline: French dockers stage one-day strike - employers.

text.p: French dockers staged a one-day strike in several key ports on Monday to protest about inadequate pay, an employers' organisation said.
France's largest ports of Le Havre and Marseille were hit, as were nine others including channel ports Calais, Boulogne and Cherbourg, the UNIM port industries association said.
The strike, which began at midnight, targeted mainly commercial traffic. Cross-channel ferry traffic to and from Britain would not be affected, an UNIM spokeswoman said.
A P&O European Ferries spokeswoman said passenger vessels were running normally.
Dockers at six ports including Dunkirk, St Nazaire and St Malo voted not to join the strike, UNIM said. Traffic at Rouen, Europe's biggest grain port, would be halted for just one hour.

The Communist-backed CGT union, which called the strike, is also organising an indefinite work-to-rule in ports involving a refusal to work overtime or do night shifts or special tasks, according to a statement released by UNIM on Monday.
The CGT union was not immediately available for comment.
A port strike would affect export shipments of agricultural products and imports of soft commodities, as well as hitting container traffic of spare parts for industry and other trade.

Marseille, one of the ports hit, is also a major oil refining centre depending on crude oil deliveries by sea. But oil flows are rarely disrupted by sporadic French port strikes, which are organised by separate union branches from oil workers.
